subject: random effects with different variances between groups

messages.author: f2b40dc7dcbe6a0c
messages.subject: random effects with different variances between groups
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to know which is the best way to introduce independent iid random effects for different groups of individuals in a multilevel (or mixed) model.

For example:

if I have an observed variable Y_ij
j=1, … , 20 (groups: for example schools)
i= 1, … , n_j (individuals for each school j)
with n_j=100 for every j

I would like to introduce random effects but considering different variances of the random effects between groups (j).

Y_ij = beta_0 + U_ij 
Where: U_ij ~ N(0, sigma^2_j)

I think one way would be:

formula <- O ~  f(id1, model="iid", …)  + f(id2, model="iid", …)   + f(id3, model="iid", …)  + ••• + f(id20, model="iid", …)
where:
id1 is a vector c(1, …, 100, NA, ..., NA )
id2 is a vector c(NA, ..., NA, 101, ..., 200, NA,...,NA)
id3 is a vector c(NA, ..., NA, 201, ..., 300, NA,...,NA)
...
id20 is a vector c(NA, ..., NA, 1901, ..., 2000)

But maybe there are more efficient (less time and memory consuming) ways … anyone can help me?

Best regards,

Rob

of what above.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random effects with different variances between groups
parts:
A matrix based suggestion to make the index set

using small n and m just to test:

n <- 3; m <- 5
ids <- kronecker(diag(n),matrix(1:m, m))
ids[ids==0] <- NA
colnames(ids) <- paste('id', 1:n, sep='')
ids

change n and m to adequate values

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] random effects with different variances between groups
parts:
And, for automatic formula construction

n <- 20
f0 <- resp ~ 1
fnew <- update(f0,
paste('.~.+', paste("f(id",1:n, ", model='iid')",
sep='', collapse='+')))
fnew

messages.author: f2b40dc7dcbe6a0c
messages.subject: Re: random effects with different variances between groups
parts:
Thank you for your answers!

But with my real data I have small areas nested in 15 regions. Moreover I want to do an independent bym model for every region. Therefore, I have to include more than 30 random effects with their respective independent variances!!.

I have tried to do this model with the Gaussian approximation and it was not possible (I think due to memory problems – I suspect that with the Laplace approximation could be nearly impossible-). So I was wondering if there was any other way. I think eventually I will have to do a more common multilevel model...

Thank you very much for your help,

Rob.
